sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year, from $22.7 billion in FY2016 to $31.7 billion in FY2025 [F198][F1][F9].
Operating income compounded faster, at 5.8% a year [F199], lifting operating margin from 22.9% [F20] to 27.2% [F28].
The sharpest break came in FY2020, when revenue fell 4.5% [D155] and operating income fell 19.9% [D156].
The filing ties the FY2020 impairment charges of $984 million [X103] primarily to the Duke Energy Progress CCR settlement [P53].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure made up 90.9% of FY2025 revenue [D541] and added 3.6pp of the 5.6% revenue growth [D543][D358].
In FY2022 the electric segment added 13.8pp of 17.1% revenue growth [D534][D239], which the filing ties to higher rate-case revenues, favorable weather and volumes [P26].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure rose 27.1% in FY2025 [D565], adding 2.0pp [D566]; the cited filings do not explain that move.
Operating costs grew 5.3% [D372] against 5.6% revenue growth [D358], an incremental operating margin of 41.4% [D378].
Diluted EPS rose 10.5% [D362], ahead of net income's 9.8% [D360], with diluted shares up only 0.6% [D374].
Operating margin of 27.2% [F28] equals its window high [D932] and sits well above the 22.9% window median [D933].
At 27.2% [F28] the margin ranks at the 75th percentile of four utility peers [D949], against a peer median of 25.7% [D950].
The FY2020 operating margin fell 3.8pp [D168] to its window low of 19.7% [D931].
Other income swung to -$1.55 billion in FY2020 [X88] from $592 million [X87], which the filing ties to lower investment returns [P55].
Net margin of 15.7% [F47] trails operating margin by 11.5pp [F28][F47]; interest expense rose to $3.63 billion in FY2025 [X63] from $3.38 billion in FY2024 [X62].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion [F77] was 2.48x net income [D346], down from 3.48x in FY2023 [D268].
Free cash flow was -$1.69 billion [F97], or -5.3% of revenue [D343]; capex of $14.0 billion [F87] ran at 1.82x D&A [D348].
Operating cash flow fell 28.5% to $5.93 billion in FY2022 [D244][F74], as the filing says under-collected fuel costs deferred to regulatory assets affected cash flows [P36].
The FY2025 10-K reports $723 million of tax-credit sale proceeds [P1]; the pack does not show which cash flow line carries them.
Net debt rose to $89.6 billion [D352] from $84.0 billion [D314], or 282.3% of revenue [D353].
Among four utility peers that ratio ranks at the 25th percentile [D953][D353], against a peer median of -228.4% [D954].
Liquidity is thin: cash and investments of $245 million [F137] cover 0.1 years of burn [D356], and the current ratio of 0.55x [F177] is close to its 0.53x window low [D943].
Debt issuance of $11.9 billion [X133] exceeded repayments of $5.65 billion [X143] in FY2025, while diluted shares rose 0.6% [D374].
Cash and investments of $245 million [F137] cover 0.1 years of the $1.69 billion FCF deficit [F97][D356], the most acute flag [R2].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x in every year of the window [D944] and is 0.55x [F177], so the flag is persistent rather than new [R1].
Net cash has fallen for nine years running [R3], reaching -$89.6 billion [D352]; the filing says capital requirements arise mainly from capex, debt repayment and dividends [P8].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2023 to FY2025 [R4], at -0.34x in FY2025 [D347].
The FY2023 revenue decline [R5] was flat: $28.7 billion [F7], against $28.7 billion in FY2022 [F6], so it is dropped as benign.
In the FY2026 10-K, free cash flow to net income below the -0.62x window median [D942] would confirm the squeeze; above the 0.01x window high [D941] would reverse it.
Net debt above $89.6 billion [D352] in the FY2026 10-K would extend the nine-year run [R3]; a level below it would reverse the trend.
In the FY2026 10-K, a current ratio below the 0.53x window low [D943] would confirm tighter liquidity; a move back toward the 0.74x high [D944] would ease it.
